# Conf42

> Conf42 runs free online tech conferences (SRE, DevOps, DevSecOps, Cloud Native, Kubernetes, Platform Engineering, Observability, LLMs, AI agents, MLOps, Golang, Python, Rust, JavaScript and more). Every talk has its own page with the video, abstract, speaker bio and transcript.

## Blog
- [All posts](https://www.conf42.com/blog): talk previews, conference roundups, sponsor keynotes, webinars
- [Every post as JSON](https://www.conf42.com/blog.json): title, Markdown URL, event, speakers, talk page, video, topics
- [Every post as Markdown links](https://www.conf42.com/blog.md)
- [LLMday Tel Aviv brings data engineering and AI agents to one room](https://www.conf42.com/blog/2026-11-09-llmday-tel-aviv-data-meets-agents): LLMday Tel Aviv, November 17 at Microsoft Reactor - free talks from FalkorDB, groundcover, Komodor, Snyk and TeraSky on agents, graphs and data.
- [LLMday Hamburg is about agents that have to ship, not demo](https://www.conf42.com/blog/2026-11-09-llmday-hamburg-agents-with-definition-of-done): LLMday Hamburg, November 18 at House of AI - 15 talks from justtrack, vCluster Labs, ScyllaDB, DKB Code Factory and more. CONF42 = 42% off.
- [Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026: when agents become platform users](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/platform-engineering-2026-roundup-agents-as-users): The Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 roundup - 26 talks on agents as platform users, delegated authority, GenAI as a platform primitive and real-time data.
- [What an engineering platform owes its AI agents](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/harness-what-platforms-owe-coding-agents): Jimmy Caputo of Harness at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on the context layer, tools, guardrails and observability agents need to ship safely.
- [Terraform and Ansible are tools; the operating model is the architecture](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/terraform-ansible-not-an-architecture): Jeleel Muibi of HybridOps at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on authority, preflight checks and run records that sit above Terraform and Ansible.
- [Power plant AI maintenance runs on context, not more sensor data](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/ai-maintenance-power-plants-context-over-data): Mohan Kumar Dalai of GE Vernova at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on AI maintenance platforms that read context, cut alarm floods and keep humans in charge.
- [Replace the system the business runs on without a big-bang weekend](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/zero-downtime-platform-migration-playbook): Saikrishna Ala (Bath and Body Works) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on dual-write, bidirectional sync and CDC as reusable migration capability.
- [Gate every automated IT fix on a confidence score](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/confidence-gated-agents-for-self-healing-ops): Madhu Chenna (Electronic Arts) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 presents ADOF, a reference architecture for self-healing IT ops with confidence-gated AI agents.
- [Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 - the prompt is the smallest part](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/prompt-engineering-2026-roundup-the-prompt-is-not-the-system): Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 in review, 18 talks on context contracts, prompt drift, injection defence, regulated workflows and agents in production.
- [Platform SLOs should stop the clock at ready, not provisioned](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/platform-slos-that-stop-the-clock-at-ready): Amith Reddy Ravuru (Reltio) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on journey SLOs that measure a developer's path from request to production-ready.
- [Your agent's evals passed. The canary is where it actually gets tested](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/agent-evals-need-a-canary-in-production): Nicolas Zelaya of Harness at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on offline evals, versioned AI configs and agent canaries as one release loop.
- [Monitoring belongs in the deploy, not in someone's memory](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/make-monitoring-a-deploy-step): Eleftheria Batsou (UptimeRobot) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on creating monitors from the pipeline with a CLI, and what still needs a human.
- [Better enterprise AI answers start before the prompt reaches the model](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/enterprise-rag-five-axes-context-before-prompt): Ravi Ray at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on a vendor-neutral five-axis framework for enterprise RAG, from ingestion to governance.
- [Model-as-a-service on Kubernetes is database-as-a-service again](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/model-as-a-service-is-database-as-a-service): Sergey Pronin (Solanica, OpenEverest) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on serving LLMs with KServe, vLLM, an AI gateway and per-key token limits.
- [Put frontend standards in the platform, not in the prompt](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/guardrails-for-ai-generated-frontends): Niharika P Pujari (McGraw Hill) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on guardrails for AI-generated frontends with design systems, Storybook, Playwright, axe-core and CI.
- [Personalised RAG should change the answer's shape, never its numbers](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/personalized-rag-same-facts-three-answers): Santosh Muthyala (Meta) at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on RAG for analytics that adapts to engineers, analysts and PMs while facts stay fixed.
- [PayPal moves the compliance gate onto the paved road with MCP](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/paypal-puts-compliance-gate-on-paved-road): Sumeet L. Ram (PayPal) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on exposing a geo-expansion platform to agents over MCP while people keep approving the rules.
- [MazeWall lets a JVM app sandbox its own threads with seccomp](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/mazewall-lets-jvm-apps-sandbox-themselves): Leanid Piliptsevich (EPAM) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 introduces MazeWall, using seccomp and Landlock to restrict pieces of an app from inside.
- [Prompt contracts catch the one-word edit that flips the meaning](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/prompt-contracts-catch-one-word-drift): Sachin Gupta (eBay) at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on prompt contracts, the schema, claim, tool and policy checks that stop prompt drift in CI.
- [T-Mobile treats the T-Life app shell as an internal platform](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/t-mobile-t-life-app-shell-as-platform): RanjithKumar Ragavan (T-Mobile) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on how five teams ship into one 53-million-user mobile app without breaking each other.
- [A plan span catches the agent that got the right answer by luck](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/agent-plan-span-catches-lucky-answers): Krishna Chaitanya Balusu (Meta) at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on OpenTelemetry plan spans for debugging agent prompts, not just answers.
- [With AI coding, the delivery bottleneck moves to code review](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/ai-coding-moves-the-bottleneck-to-review): Lucas Mazei (Memed) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 applies the theory of constraints to AI-assisted delivery and shows where platform teams should push.
- [A detailed prompt still doesn't make the answer correct](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/prompt-engineering-is-evaluating-the-output): Emmanuela Opurum (SoftNet Technologies) at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on templates, .md rule files and evaluating every AI response.
- [A platform team of one runs side projects with AI, not on AI](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/platform-team-of-one-ai-side-projects): Shem Magnezi (Lemonade) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on running many AI-built side projects alone with minimal launches, recoverable paths and agents.
- [The smallest internal platform: a plugin-based Dev Mode for Android](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/robofinance-dev-mode-plugin-framework-android): Denis Galkin (Robofinance) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on turning scattered debug menus into a plugin-based Dev Mode framework inside the app.
- [A looping agent keeps every dashboard green](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/agentcore-datadog-loops-burn-tokens-silently): Indika Wimalasuriya (Virtusa) at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 traces a Bedrock AgentCore agent end to end in Datadog, kill switch included.
- [Kafka won't make your retail supply chain resilient on its own](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/kafka-wont-make-your-supply-chain-resilient): Nidhin Jose (Walmart) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on the ownership, idempotency and recovery patterns that make event-driven retail systems hold up.
- [Five LLMs taught a small model to spot 70 kinds of news bias](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/llms-as-teachers-for-news-bias-model): Aleem Khan at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on replacing five LLM API calls per story with an owned model trained on expert-checked labels.
- [In real-time bidding, a late answer is a no answer](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/in-real-time-bidding-late-means-no): Sujan Challa (Samsung Electronics America) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on building an ad auction platform around a 100 ms latency wall.
- [Conf42 Feature Flags 2026: kill switches, migrations and model gates](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/conf42-feature-flags-2026-roundup): Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 roundup: 16 talks from Harness, Capital One, Adobe, Bank of America, Confluent and more on flags for AI agents, migrations and models.
- [Debezium Platform turns CDC from a ticket queue into self-service](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/debezium-platform-ends-cdc-ticket-queue): Vincenzo Santonastaso (IBM, Debezium maintainer) at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on scaling change data capture across teams with Debezium Platform.
- [Feature flags turn a migration into a ramp you can walk back down](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/feature-flags-make-migrations-reversible): Ryan Vila of Harness at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on gradual, measurable, reversible cloud-native migrations, and the flag hygiene that keeps them safe.
- [From prompt to product starts long before the first prompt](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/prompt-to-product-starts-before-the-prompt): LaShawnda Rodgers (RGLC) at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on taking an app from Reddit research and a PRD through AI builders to launch.
- [BetBoom's own Dota 2 draft feed took conversion from 8.4% to 31.2%](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/betboom-built-its-own-dota-2-draft-feed): Egor Kolovertnykh of BetBoom at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on turning Dota 2 Game State Integration snapshots into a live draft feed.
- [A customer-facing agent got reliable outside its prompt](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/customer-facing-agent-reliability-outside-prompt): Nowlun's Ahmed Gaber and Ahmed Morsi at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on clean data, code-held rules and staged evals for a freight sales copilot.
- [Treat tokens like money: a GenAI gateway with budget holds](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/genai-platform-gateway-budget-holds-cache-failover): Brindal Patel of Coinbase at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on a GenAI gateway with card-style token budgets, safe semantic caching and eval-gated failover.
- [Your rollout guardrail can look healthy after its calibration expired](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/guardrail-calibration-expires-mid-rollout): Rakshay Pawar of Codeflow Capital at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 uses a 35-year Treasury yield backtest to show why clustered misses break rollout guardrails.
- [Pack five metrics into one LLM judge call, but not forty](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/packing-llm-judge-metrics-cost-accuracy): Scarlett Attensil of LaunchDarkly at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on how many criteria one LLM judge can score before accuracy slips.
- [Code Mode cut an MCP agent's tool context from 150K to 22K tokens](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/mcp-code-mode-150k-to-22k-tokens): Adobe's Nishant Kumar Thakur and Sonam Raj at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on typed tool stubs for MCP, what they saved and where they broke.
- [A first talk on feature flags: deploy is not release](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/feature-flags-primer-deploy-is-not-release): SoftNet Technologies' Emmanuela Opurum at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 gives a beginner-friendly tour of flags, rollouts, canaries, blue-green, A/B tests and flag hygiene.
- [The feature store behind every For You feed, explained](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/feature-store-infra-behind-for-you-pages): Attila Toth of ScyllaDB at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on online feature stores, P99 tail latency, query-first data models and pluggable stores.
- [Single-layer LLM guardrails miss attacks spread across turns](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/single-layer-guardrails-miss-multi-turn-attacks): Manvitha Potluri at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 tested 390 prompts on AWS Bedrock; a second intent layer caught what keyword filters missed.
- [A correct diagnosis doesn't give an AI agent the authority to act](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/ai-agents-need-delegated-authority-not-permissions): Ruby Agarwal, VP of Engineering at Avaya, at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on scoped, expiring authority for agents that remediate production.
- [A Claw is a coding agent that never logs off](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/personal-coding-agent-claws-explained): Erik Hanchett of AWS at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on Claws, the always-on coding agents with memory, schedules, chat apps and sandboxes.
- [In anti-money laundering work, a prompt is a compliance control](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/aml-prompt-is-a-compliance-control): Pratik Patel of Hexaware at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on grounded, schema-checked prompts for AML investigations that never infer intent.
- [Agent engineering starts by assuming the model gets fooled](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/agent-engineering-assume-the-model-gets-fooled): Cynthia Akiotu of Accenture at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on identity, MCP tools and authorization checks that hold when prompt injection works.
- [Self-healing infrastructure should automate certainty, escalate ambiguity](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/automate-certainty-escalate-ambiguity-flags): Confluent's Prateek Jindal at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on feature flags as infrastructure controls in a detect, decide, recover, validate loop.
- [Physical AI safety agents should reason over a system graph](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/physical-ai-safety-agents-system-graph): Vraj Patel of Apptronik at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on bounded agents, system graphs and skills for safety assurance in robots and AVs.
- [Your agent orchestrator won't save your money; the thin controller will](https://www.conf42.com/blog/platform2026/agent-orchestrator-thin-controller-saves-money): Yedidya Schwartz, CTO of Quicklizard, at Conf42 Platform Engineering 2026 on crashing six durable engines to see who pays twice for model calls.
- [Put AI inside the release loop, not on a dashboard after the fact](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/ai-belongs-in-sdlc-not-dashboard): Amazon's Naveen Goel at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on per-PR efficiency checks, gated release waves and bounded AI authority to catch quiet regressions.
- [NEPA permitting with LLMs needs prompts that act like governed rules](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/nepa-permitting-prompts-as-governed-rules): Mohit Upadhyay of Tech Mahindra at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 on evidence-first prompts, provenance and RAG for NEPA categorical exclusions.
- [A solo dev forced his LLM failover live and found four ladders](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/forced-llm-failover-one-kv-flag): Fuad Laguda at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on a three-state Cloudflare KV trace flag and a deliberately forced failover from Claude Sonnet to Qwen on Nebius.
- [Give an agent's Terraform change consequences before merge](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/simulate-terraform-change-before-merge): Kevin Brown of Cloud World Model at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 shows simulated cost, CPU and latency for an infrastructure PR, gaps labelled.
- [Conf42 DevSecOps 2026 roundup: checking agents before they act](https://www.conf42.com/blog/devsecops2026/devsecops-2026-roundup-agents-at-the-gate): Conf42 DevSecOps 2026 in review, from hooks that gate coding agents and SBOMs that stop at the model to cell isolation, masking checks and safe recovery.
- [Auto-healing APIs need feature flags and brakes, not just restarts](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/auto-healing-apis-need-flags-and-brakes): Anil Kumar Chitiprolu at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on a control loop that pairs monitoring, circuit breakers and feature flags to recover microservices safely.
- [Your coding agent's dotfiles are the new software supply chain](https://www.conf42.com/blog/devsecops2026/agent-dotfiles-new-supply-chain-harness): Roshan Piyush of Harness at Conf42 DevSecOps 2026 on why hooks, skills, memory and MCP servers are where AI supply chain attacks now land.
- [Charter, harness, factory: who owns each coding agent rule](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/coding-agent-rules-charter-harness-factory): Ian Johnson of Parento at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 maps where a coding agent gate can sit and who gets paged when that rule is wrong.
- [Your agent's prompt is one layer, not the whole system](https://www.conf42.com/blog/prompt2026/agent-prompt-is-one-layer-not-the-system): Emerson Braun of Plan A Technologies at Conf42 Prompt Engineering 2026 splits agent reliability into six layers so a fix lands in the right one.
- [Feature flags manage exposure, quality gates decide if AI earns it](https://www.conf42.com/blog/featureflags2026/genai-quality-gates-decide-flag-exposure): Adobe's Rajesh Lingam at Conf42 Feature Flags 2026 on three evaluation gates that decide when a GenAI feature behind a flag gets more traffic.
- [Verify AI-written code inside the agent's loop, not at the gate](https://www.conf42.com/blog/devsecops2026/verify-ai-code-inside-agent-loop-not-gate): At Conf42 DevSecOps 2026, TestSprite co-founder Yunhao Jiao argues coding agents need runtime checks while they work, using the CoderCup experiment.
